h1: Update Udyam Registration — Keep Your Details Accurate

aiOverview.short: To update your Udyam Registration, log in to the official Udyam portal using your Registration Number and OTP verification, then edit the relevant fields such as turnover, investment, address or business activity, and resubmit. Updated details are reflected on a fresh certificate once processed.
aiOverview.medium: Updating your Udyam Registration involves logging into the official Udyam portal using your Udyam Registration Number along with OTP verification through your registered mobile number. Once logged in, you can edit fields such as annual turnover, investment in plant or machinery, business address, main business activity, and NIC code. This is important because your classification as micro, small or medium is based on turnover and investment figures, which can change as your business grows. After submitting updates, the system reprocesses your details, and a revised certificate reflecting the accurate information becomes available for download.
aiOverview.long:
Updating your Udyam Registration is necessary whenever key details about your business change, most commonly your annual turnover or investment in plant, machinery or equipment, since these directly affect your MSME classification as micro, small or medium. The process is done through the official Udyam portal, where you log in using your Udyam Registration Number and verify your identity through an OTP sent to your registered mobile number. Once logged in, you can edit various fields including business address, main business activity, NIC code, and financial figures. It is important to keep these details current, since outdated information can cause issues when your certificate is used for loan applications, tenders or government scheme submissions. After submitting your updates, the portal reprocesses the application, and once approved, a revised certificate reflecting the corrected details becomes available for download, replacing the earlier version.

body.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: Businesses grow, change addresses, add new activities, and see their turnover shift year to year. When any of this happens, your Udyam Registration needs to reflect the current reality of your business, not the numbers you entered when you first registered. This guide explains exactly what can be updated, how to do it, and when it becomes necessary.

body.heading: Why You Might Need to Update Your Udyam Registration
paragraphs: The most common reasons businesses update their registration include a change in annual turnover or investment figures that affects their MSME classification, a change in business address, the addition of new business activities, or correction of an error that was made during the original registration.

body.heading: What Details Can Be Updated
paragraphs: You can typically update your business address, main business activity and NIC code, turnover figures, investment in plant, machinery or equipment, and certain organisational details. Some core identifiers, like the PAN used for registration, generally cannot simply be edited and may require a fresh registration if they need to change.

body.heading: Step by Step Guide to Update Udyam Registration
paragraphs: The process begins with logging into the official Udyam portal using your existing Udyam Registration Number, followed by OTP verification on your registered mobile number. Once logged in, you can navigate to the relevant section, make the necessary edits, and submit the updated application for processing.

body.heading: Updating Turnover and Investment Figures
paragraphs: Since your classification as micro, small or medium is based on combined turnover and investment figures, it is important to update these regularly, particularly if your business has grown. An outdated classification can create complications if a bank, tender authority, or government scheme cross checks your figures against other financial records.

body.heading: Correcting Business Name, Address or Activity
paragraphs: If your registered business name, address, or primary activity has changed or was entered incorrectly, these details can generally be corrected through the update process. Once submitted, the corrected information appears on your revised certificate.

body.heading: Common Issues While Updating
paragraphs: Some business owners face difficulties updating their registration due to OTP verification issues, incorrect entry of new figures that create fresh mismatches with GST or income tax records, or confusion about which fields can and cannot be edited directly.

body.heading: How Often Should You Update Your Registration
paragraphs: There is no fixed schedule, but it is good practice to review and update your Udyam Registration whenever there is a meaningful change in your business, particularly after your annual turnover is finalised each year, or after any change in business address or activity.

paragraphs: Business owners often ask whether updating their registration creates a new registration number, how long an update takes to process, and whether old certificates remain valid until the update is approved. These are addressed in the FAQ section.

A few minutes spent updating outdated details can prevent much bigger complications later.

faq.question: Does updating my Udyam Registration change my registration number?
faq.answer: No, your Udyam Registration Number generally remains the same, only the details on your certificate are revised.

faq.question: Is there a fee to update my Udyam Registration?
faq.answer: No, updates on the official portal are free.

faq.question: Can I update my PAN on an existing Udyam Registration?
faq.answer: Core PAN details generally cannot be changed directly and may require a fresh registration under the correct PAN.

faq.question: Does my classification change automatically when I update turnover?
faq.answer: Yes, your classification is recalculated based on the updated figures.

faq.question: What if my update request gets stuck?
faq.answer: This is usually due to a data mismatch, which needs to be identified and corrected before the update can proceed.
